what: truncated indexed MKV and MP4 sources produced shortened outputs with completed and verified true
escaped: ffmpeg logged premature EOF but exited zero, so output probing accepted a readable shortened encode and stream fallback treated the attempt as successful
mechanism: runner completion rejects the specific demuxer premature-EOF and indexed partial-file diagnostics before promotion or fallback, for captured and progress writes alike; generated MKV and MP4 fixtures pin the refusal, cleanup, overwrite preservation and clean controls while explicit repair and optional analysis keep their measured-damage behavior

what: four merged PRs with a new flag, new result fields and two fixes were not released: they carried only the chore label
escaped: the release version was decided from PR labels, and the labels from the PR title
mechanism: resolve_version.py takes a floor from the tree: shipped code changed is a patch, a contract that gained a name is a minor (test_release_version_resolver_does_not_depend_on_a_pr_title)

what: font_used named an installed fallback for a fontconfig alias to an uninstalled directory face, or a bitmap-only directory face libass rejected
escaped: directory tests covered literal names and styles, not aliases or non-outline faces; a directory miss was assumed equivalent to no directory
mechanism: the shared directory scanner accepts only verified outline faces and preserves unknown metadata for coverage callers; directory misses report no established file instead of a global fc-match guess, with real alias and bitmap burns and missing-outline controls

what: a still named with a % that is not a pattern failed in ffmpeg (Option pattern_type not found), and a relative subtitle path whose first segment has a colon failed with Protocol not found
escaped: the two escapes were written for the cases that had been reported (a %d pattern, an absolute path) and tested only with those names
mechanism: runner's still-input arguments always open a % name as one image2 file, and decision.escape_filter_path writes ./ before every relative path a filter option takes, so every tool that reads a still or passes a file to a filter goes through the same two functions
size_reason: 4.0.0 carries the caller-visible changes held since #632 in one release; the maintainer chose to raise the code ceiling once for them (#632, 2026-11-19)

what: an empty file, a directory, a non-media file or one the user may not read gave ffprobe's raw lines or 'input not found'; a name starting with a dash reached ffprobe as an option; an extension the build has no muxer for failed in ffmpeg after a dry run that completed
escaped: each tool checked only that the input path existed, and the output extension only against the skill's own list
mechanism: probe() refuses an unusable input by reason (input_empty, input_is_directory, input_not_media) before any tool reads it, runner.refuse_denied_input names a permission error the same way for every tool, a dash name is passed as ./name by the one function that builds input arguments, and runner checks an output extension against the build's own muxer list before ffmpeg runs

what: export.py wrote a single-file video delivery that missed the preset's codec, size, frame rate, duration or --max-mb limit and exited 0 with verified false
escaped: verified was computed and reported, but nothing turned a failed required property into a failed run
mechanism: export.py compares the written file's probe with the preset's required properties after every encode and fails the run with kind verification when one is missed; the test redirects the real encoder to a wrong size and checks the exit status

what: fit.py --duration with no method retimed a 103.8 s clip to 60 s at 1.73x, where the caller may have meant a trim
escaped: the large_speed_change warning was the only signal, and a warning does not stop a run
mechanism: fit.py refuses an implicit retime beyond 1.15x in either direction with fit_method_required before ffmpeg runs, dry runs included, so the caller states the method; render.py forwards a project clip's explicit speed as --method speed

what: a delivery template rendered an all-black source and reported it verified: the content checks (black frames, freezes, silence, dropouts) were never run
escaped: check.content was off unless a project set it, and no shipped template set it
mechanism: every shipped template sets check.content, and a test reads all ten templates for it, so a new template without it fails

what: fit.py --fit crop warned crop_content_off_centre on motion spread evenly over the frame and suggested the --crop-x already in use
escaped: the motion rule compared motion_outside with a fixed 0.5 while the detail rule compared with the discarded share; the tests had a box at the edge and a box in the centre, never motion over the whole frame
mechanism: both rules now measure an excess over the discarded share, and the warning drops a remedy equal to the anchor in use; a whole-frame motion case and a both-edges case pin it

what: join.py --copy of AAC clips let the sound fall about 32 ms further behind the picture at each join and reported the join lossless
escaped: the copy join checked that the streams matched but never measured where each clip's decoded sound ends against its picture; the tests joined two clips, where the drift stays under the 50 ms tolerance
mechanism: the join predicts the delay from each clip's measured priming and decoded-audio length and refuses when it crosses COPY_AV_GAP at any clip; the prediction is pinned against the measured drift at 2, 3 and 8 clips
size_reason: the prediction needs a decode of each clip's audio; a refusal alone could not say at which clip the join breaks

what: waveform.py --at accepted --fps, --silence-threshold, --quality, --fast and the audiogram layout flags and did nothing with them
escaped: --at refused a hand-kept list of options, which missed every flag added to the video path after it
mechanism: the refusal reads the parser: any flag in WAVEFORM_VIDEO_ONLY that differs from its default is named, so a flag added there is refused without a second list

what: loudness.py (and export --normalize) wrote a sound whose timestamps jumped about 0.1 s after digital silence: each later beep played 89 ms after its flash and the end was cut
escaped: loudness.py's tests measured the level and the length, never where a sound sits against its picture; export's A/V tests ran without --normalize until 4.0.0 made it the default
mechanism: the loudnorm pass restamps its samples (asetpts=N/SR/TB+STARTPTS), and a flash/beep test checks loudness.py's output against its picture and for any timestamp jump

what: loudness.py (and export's default normalise) closed a gap in the source's sound: with 0.8 s of sound missing, every later beep played early against the copied picture (measured on FFmpeg 6.1, dynamic mode; 85 ms early for an 80 ms gap in both modes once a first fix was in)
escaped: the gap test checked packet times in linear mode on FFmpeg 6.1 only, where loudnorm passes them through; dynamic mode, a gap under swresample's 100 ms threshold and other builds were not measured
mechanism: the gap is filled with silence before both loudnorm passes (aresample=async=1:min_hard_comp=0.01), and the test checks flash against beep after an 80 ms and a 0.8 s gap in both modes, on every build CI runs

what: the review page read its data back out of the document as text and put values that came from an element's attribute or a field (the selected number, a flag's key, a tool's name, the overlay colour) into markup as they were
escaped: the page was checked in a browser with the project's own names only, and CI has no browser; the first scan of the template found it
mechanism: the data is the script's own value (window.REVIEW_DATA), never read from the DOM; every value that re-enters markup goes through esc(), which now covers both quotes; an action, a language, a tab, a colour, a platform and a selected number are accepted only when they are ones the page knows; the logo is cloned from its template instead of being read as text

what: under --engine auto, with no language named or detectable and no Whisper engine able to run, the English-only Parakeet model transcribed the speech anyway: Japanese came out as English words with verified: true and a note
escaped: the note was the decided behaviour (#305): a caller that reads verified, and a person who reads the result after the captions are burned, never saw it
mechanism: an English-only model does not run on a language nobody measured or named: _parakeet_attempt() passes it over before it runs and the existing english_only refusal lists it with the flag that names the language, for caption.py and silence.py alike; the note, its warning kind and the notes plumbing are removed

what: the first release after the hand-bumped 4.0.0 failed in the bump step (CHANGELOG.md has no '## Unreleased' section), so the merged changes were not published
escaped: a hand bump writes its own section on top and removes the Unreleased heading, test_changelog_has_one_heading_per_version allows that shape, and the bump step was only ever read as text by the tests, never run on it
mechanism: the bump step takes a CHANGELOG with no Unreleased section (the new section goes above the first version heading), and a test runs the step's own lines, cut from release.yml, on both shapes and on a file with no heading

what: an agent that guessed an option's name was told only that it was unrecognized, or (when a required option was also missing) nothing about it at all: straighten.py --angle 5 answered 'the following arguments are required: --degrees'; overlay.py --position bottom-center answered 'bad --position' with no list of the names
escaped: every tool's usage error is argparse's own, which names the bad token and never the option that was meant, and no test typed a plausible wrong name: the tests call each tool the way its author spells it
mechanism: one shared step (runner._teach, on every tool's parser) names, for each --flag the tool lacks, its nearest option, the options whose help uses the word, and the tools that do take it; docs/stumbles.jsonl records each first-try stumble and StumbleLedgerTests replays every taught line, so a new stumble is one line and a test

what: freeze.py --time 3 --hold 1 ran: argparse read --time as --timeout (it takes any unambiguous start of an option name), so the run had a 3 second time limit, froze the last frame instead of the one at 3 s, and said nothing
escaped: argparse's default (allow_abbrev) was never a decision here, and no test typed an option name that is the start of another; it was found by running 126 calls written by an agent that had seen only each tool's name
mechanism: apply_common refuses a shortened name of an option every tool shares (--timeout, --overwrite, --dry-run, --plan, ...) and names the full one; a tool's own options keep the shortening, which callers use. test_a_shortened_shared_option_is_refused_and_a_tools_own_is_kept pins both halves, and the stumble is a taught line in docs/stumbles.jsonl

what: a number no file can have was taken: cropdetect.py --samples 1000000000 and graphics.py --template countdown --from 1000000000 gave no answer, caption.py --size -1 and overlay.py --font-size 1000000000 wrote a file, scenes.py --threshold -1 ran against a help that said 0-100, and fit.py --width 1000000000 failed inside ffmpeg with 'Cannot allocate memory', which names no option
escaped: each tool checked the options its author thought of, one check per option, and the tests give an option the values it was written for; no step looked at every number, so 213 of 558 edge calls (0, -1 and 1000000000 on each numeric option of 28 tools) ran
mechanism: apply_common reads every numeric option after parsing: a range the help states as a..b is the range taken, a negative is refused unless the help names one (-N, dB, degrees, stops), and nothing but --length-samples is past a million. The ranges that were missing are written in the help (cropdetect --samples 1..100, graphics --from 0..600, overlay --font-size 1..2000, audio --gain -96..96, the widths 1..16384), which is all the fix they needed. test_a_number_outside_what_its_option_takes_is_refused_on_every_tool gives the reported values, the values that must still run, and reads every stated range against its own default; tests/edge_values.py now shows 454 refused, 104 ran, 0 hung

what: the name decided for a thing was refused by the tools that hold an older one: straighten.py --angle 2, freeze.py --duration 2, caption.py --font-size 40, stabilize.py --strength 6 and six more answered with a hint and did not run, so an agent that guessed the decided name needed a second call, and a small model often did not make it
escaped: 4.1.1 decided the names and taught them in the usage error, and held the renaming for the feature freeze; a hint was treated as equal to a name that runs, and nothing measured the difference until the same 126 blind calls were given to low-cost models (two of 126 ran on an 8B model)
mechanism: the decided name is a second spelling of the option the tool already has (argparse option strings, no new code): ten options on eight tools. The freeze guard lets a spelling through and nothing else (feature_freeze_spellings, the owner's decision), a stumble whose guess became a spelling is marked named and replayed so it is never called unknown again, and test_the_decided_name_and_the_older_one_are_the_same_option compares the plan of both spellings

what: a position at an exact half frame was rounded to even: 0.5 s at 25 fps (12.5 frames) became frame 12 in the timeline, the EDL's source timecode and the output's start timecode, one frame off the same cut made by decision.py or by a tool that follows velisa/timebase@1 TB-4
escaped: timeline.py used Python's round(), which rounds a half to even, in four places, while decision.py and FFmpeg's av_rescale round a half up; the tests used positions that are whole frames or clear of a half
mechanism: every count of frames in timeline.py is floor(x + 1/2) on Fractions (the frame helper, the clip length, the EDL's source out and the start timecode's offset, contributed in #644; and the speed-scaled source start and end in the FCPXML and OTIO exporters, three more places the sweep found); test_a_half_frame_position_rounds_up gives 0.5 s at 25 fps, one frame at 2x, a 0.02 s offset and a 7-frame handle at 1.5x in both exporters. What is left as round() there is a frame rate's nominal integer, not a position

what: render.py --cache DIR --dry-run created DIR and wrote and removed a file named .writable in it, so a dry run changed the disk and deleted a caller's file of that name
escaped: the writability probe of the cache ran before the dry-run branch, and the dry-run test only looked at the directory's listing after the run, which was empty either way
mechanism: in a dry run the cache directory is only inspected (it may be absent; a path that is not a directory is still refused), and the real run probes with a NamedTemporaryFile, which cannot collide with a file a caller owns; the tests put a sentinel named .writable in the cache and read it back after a real run and a dry run. Contributed in #561

what: join.py --copy measured a stream's span from the head and the tail of the file; where ffprobe exits 0 after the head read and returns no tail packets, the span ended early and a long clip was reported shorter than it is
escaped: the span reader trusted two read intervals and never checked that the second one had been honoured; the fixtures were short enough for the head read to cover them
mechanism: _stream_span reads every packet again when the clip is longer than three tail windows and the result has no more packets than the head read can return, or ends before the tail window; tests cover the head-only answer, a sparse low-frame-rate clip and an audio stream. Contributed in #567

what: an output name that makes ffmpeg write files it names itself was handed on: -o out.m3u8 wrote out0.ts, -o out.mpd wrote init-stream0.m4s, -o frame%03d.png wrote frame001.png onward (H.264 bytes under .png names); files of those names that existed were replaced without --overwrite, and the tool reported a failure only afterwards
escaped: every output guard (exists, is an input, locked, staged) looks at the one path the caller named, and ffmpeg's -y covers whatever the muxer derives from it; the tests name outputs with single-file extensions
mechanism: _check_output_path, which every ffmpeg command and every sidecar passes before anything runs, refuses a playlist extension (.m3u8, .m3u, .mpd) and a numbered pattern in an image name, with the existing reason output_extension_unsupported; -update (look.py, scenes.py) and a literal percent in another container's name are left alone. test_an_output_ffmpeg_would_split_into_files_it_names_is_refused runs seven calls over files that must stay byte-identical. Reported in #562; #568 by zfareed worked the full analysis this follows

what: a wrong call was answered with advice and the caller had to build the right one: denoise.py --strength strong listed the three choices, silence.py --threshold -30dB said 'expected one argument', cut.py --strat 1 named --start; and three shapes most models wrote had no option at all (proxy.py --height 360, redact.py --rect X:Y:W:H, metadata.py --chapter TIME=TITLE)
escaped: the answers were written for a reader who reasons from a hint; the measurement that showed otherwise came later: nine models on 126 blind tasks, where a second attempt after reading the answer doubled what ran for a 26B model but an 8B one still failed most, and where the same three missing shapes came from most models
mechanism: runner._teach ends the usage error with `try:` and the whole corrected command when every mistake on the line has one answer (a near option, a choice's near neighbour or common other word, a number written with its unit), and prints nothing when one does not; the three shapes are options. test_a_mistake_with_one_answer_is_followed_by_the_corrected_command runs each corrected command, and test_three_things_most_models_asked_for_are_options_now measures the three outputs. tests/first_try.py gives a blind call a two-minute clip and real stand-in files, so a refusal counts against the call and not against the harness

what: on FFmpeg 9.1 a command that writes AAC could run until its time limit and leave a 48-byte file: sync.py --replace-audio with a second file that starts 0.1 s or 2.5 s late (mono, 192k) never returned on Windows, where the package feed had moved to 9.1.0 the same day
escaped: 9.1 changed the AAC encoder's default coder (nmr) and the suite's version of FFmpeg on Windows is whatever the feed serves: the first run on it was a pull request that changed an error message, and its three jobs were cancelled at 75 minutes with nothing naming the command; every tool writes AAC at a fixed 192k whatever the channel count, the case the new coder does not return from
mechanism: runner.pin_aac_coder, on the path every ffmpeg command takes (run), names the coder that was the default until 9.0 (`-aac_coder twoloop`) from 9.1 on, unless the command names one; older builds get the command they always got. .github/workflows/ffmpeg-next.yml reads the newest FFmpeg on demand with a probe that puts a time limit on each call and lists what is left running, and CI installs a pinned version so a feed update arrives as a change someone makes; three tests that added up AAC packet durations count a packet as the smaller of its duration and its frame less the stated discard, which holds for the three ways 6.1, 9.0 and 9.1 write the end of a track

what: a clip of one shape exported into a preset of the other was written mostly as bars and nothing said so: a 720x1280 clip through export.py --preset youtube came out 1920x1080 with the picture 32% of the frame, status completed, verified true; the same for a 1280x720 clip into reels and for fit.py --aspect 9:16 with its default pad
escaped: the checks compare the file with the preset's frame, and the frame was met; no test exported a clip into a preset of another shape and asked what the caller was told, and the workflow leaves that to a look at the picture the caller makes afterwards
mechanism: decision.pad_filters, the one place export.py and fit.py build a solid-colour pad, warns (picture_small_in_frame: fraction, source, frame) when the picture fills less than half of the frame, naming --fit crop and the presets of the other shape; a blurred background and a crop say nothing; the default stays pad

what: look.py --at wrote every frame at --width (default 1280) whatever the source: a 720x1280 clip's frame came out 1280x2276, interpolated, 2.1 to 2.4 MB a frame where the source's own pixels are under 1 MB
escaped: --width was written for the contact sheet, whose width is a layout choice, and reused for a single frame, where it is a resampling of the evidence; the tests take frames from clips at least as wide as the width they pass
mechanism: a single --at frame is scaled to min(--width, the source's displayed width): --width bounds it and never enlarges it; sheets and --compare images keep the width asked; test_a_frame_taken_to_look_at_is_not_enlarged

what: on Windows the MCP server answered no tools/call until the client closed stdin, from 3.10.0 to 4.3.4: the tool ran and wrote its output, and the JSON-RPC response was written only when the client hung up, so a client that waits for the answer waited for ever
escaped: 3.10.0 moved tools/call to a worker thread while the main thread keeps reading stdin; the worker's child (a sibling Python script) inherited the server's stdin, the client's pipe, and on Windows did not finish exiting while it was open. Every stdio test closed stdin before reading the tool's answer, and no test ran a tool call on Windows with the pipe still open
mechanism: run_tool, verify.py's step runner and child_kwargs (every ffmpeg/ffprobe child started through it) give the child stdin=DEVNULL; test_mcp_answers_a_tool_call_while_the_client_keeps_its_pipe_open reads the answer to a tools/call before closing stdin, on every CI platform, and checks the three spawn points

what: twenty options (--preset on eight tools, overlay's and graphics' colour and font options, caption --bold, join/export --pad-color, look --no-timecode, multicam's --max-offset and --analyze-seconds) had no help, so --help and the MCP tool descriptions left an agent to guess their values
escaped: help text is optional in argparse and nothing checked it; the tools that did document these options (sync, scenes, fit, broll, grid) were never compared with the ones that did not
mechanism: test_every_option_has_help_text walks every tool's input_schema in the contract and fails an option with no description, so a new option cannot ship without one

what: a time written to the millisecond just after a frame's start was cut as the next frame: at 30000/1001, cut.py --start 1.902 kept 32 frames and --start 1.9019 kept 33, --end 1.902 kept 58 and 1.9019 kept 57, so a caller that rounds frame-exact boundaries to milliseconds got one frame more or fewer than planned
escaped: grid_at_or_after took a time to the next frame unless it was within a millionth of a frame past one, which is true of the exact time and not of a time rounded to a millisecond (up to 0.5 ms, about 0.015 frame, later); cut's single-range re-encode passed its times to -ss and -t without using the grid at all, and the tests gave frame-exact or mid-frame times
mechanism: cut.py cuts each start and end on the nearest frame when that frame is within half a millisecond either way, before any mode runs, and requested_start/requested_end stay what was asked; the shared grid_at_or_after is unchanged (a tolerance there turned fit.py --duration 1.0014 at 25 fps from 26 frames into 25, which test_a_window_or_a_length_on_a_frame_time_keeps_that_frame caught), so freeze.py --at 1.902 still holds the following frame and is left for its own change; test_a_time_given_in_milliseconds_is_read_back_to_its_frame compares the millisecond and the exact time for --start and --end on a 30000/1001 clip

what: a 1280x720 clip made 9:16 with fit.py --aspect 9:16 came out 406x720 with nothing said about the size, and the routing table's own example gave that command; a frame larger than the picture (fit with a size, an export preset above the clip's size) was enlarged with swscale's default
escaped: keeping the source's size under --aspect is a decision (an earlier version enlarged 3x unasked), and the decision stopped at the size: nothing told a caller that a delivery frame of that shape is 1080x1920, and no test looked at how an enlargement is made
mechanism: fit.py notes the frame it wrote and the --width that gives the usual delivery frame when --aspect alone made the frame smaller than the source; decision.enlarge_args adds -sws_flags lanczos to fit.py and export.py commands whose frame is larger than the picture, and nothing otherwise; SKILL.md's vertical row asks for --width 1080

what: the siblings of #653: freeze.py --at 1.902, broll.py --at 1.902 and a speedramp.py segment bound at 1.902 read the time as the frame after the one at 1.9019 (30000/1001), so the hold, the cutaway and the speed change each began one frame late for a caller that rounds frame times to milliseconds
escaped: the fix for #653 moved the time in cut.py only; the sweep that would have found the other three was written down as left for later instead of run
mechanism: decision.on_frame (the nearest frame within half a millisecond, never one before the first) is the one place a named position is read, used by cut.py, freeze.py --at, broll.py --at and its end, and speedramp.py's bounds; grid_at_or_after is unchanged because a length (fit.py --duration) also goes through it; test_a_position_given_in_milliseconds_is_its_frame_in_the_tools_that_take_one compares the command built for 1.902 with the one for 1.9019 in each tool and measures freeze's held frame

what: font_used.substituted was false where no face was established: caption.py --fonts-dir with no face of the asked name (or an unreadable folder, or other styles only), --ass, and a family ffmpeg or libass looks up by name all reported file null beside substituted false, which reads as 'not substituted' to a caller that keys on the field
escaped: the value was a default written next to file: null, and the contract's own text had to explain that false was not a measured absence there
mechanism: substituted is null wherever file is null (caption.py's unresolved --fonts-dir paths and --ass, fonts.font_choice's by_name), false only for an established face of the asked family, true for another family; the schema text and docs/contract.md say so, and the fonts_dir tests expect null for a folder without the face

what: a stream-copied cut that landed 0.1 s past what was asked reported verified: true, with the miss in duration_error_ms further down the document; in the 24-request benchmark models read the top of the document and reported the cut as the length asked
escaped: the result document was written for a program (probe.duration, expected_duration, duration_error_ms as separate fields) and verified says the file is sound, not that it is the length asked; nothing in the first lines said either number
mechanism: emit() puts `wrote` first after status for every media file written: the measured length, `(ASKED N s: M s longer|shorter)` when it misses expected_duration by more than 40 ms, the frame and rate, and what the file holds; test_the_first_line_of_a_result_says_what_was_written_and_where_it_misses pins the order, the miss on a copied cut, its absence on an accurate one and under --dry-run

what: proxy, denoise, crop, redact, straighten and sphere --fps 50 on a 25 fps source starting 01:00:00:12 wrote 01:00:00:12 into the 50 fps output, a label that names 0.24 s instead of 0.48 s; fit.py had been fixed alone
escaped: the relabel was added to fit.py's own command line, and the other tools that take --fps force the rate through decision.cfr_args without passing it
mechanism: decision.cfr_args adds output_timecode_args at the forced rate when --fps differs from the source's, and run_keeping_subtitles skips copying the source's tmcd track whenever the command writes its own label, so every tool that forces a rate there relabels; test_every_tool_that_takes_fps_counts_the_start_timecode_at_it runs the six tools at 50 and 25

what: audio.py with the picture kept (--voice, --music, --replace and the rest) wrote the sound as stream 0 and the picture as stream 1
escaped: the filter graph's output was mapped before the copied picture, and no test read the stream order
mechanism: the picture is mapped first; test_the_picture_stays_stream_0_and_a_multichannel_a_roll_keeps_its_channels reads the order, and a sweep of 23 writing tools found no other that puts the sound first

what: broll.py --audio b and --audio mix folded a 5.1 A-roll to stereo, verified: true, nothing said
escaped: the mix was built at a fixed stereo layout for every input
mechanism: an A-roll with more than two channels keeps its layout through the mix and the cutaway's sound is up-mixed to it; mono and stereo A-rolls are mixed in stereo as before

what: --fit crop to a frame of the other shape cut away most of the picture and said nothing: a 1920x1080 clip through export.py --preset reels --fit crop, fit.py --aspect 9:16 --fit crop or join.py --fit crop into 1080x1920 kept the centre 32% with no warning
escaped: #666 added picture_small_in_frame for the pad and noted the crop sibling without sweeping it
mechanism: decision.warn_mostly_cropped, called where fit, export and join build their crop, warns picture_mostly_cropped with the fraction kept below one half; test_a_crop_that_keeps_less_than_half_of_the_picture_is_said checks the three tools and two crops that keep more

what: a source's chapters stayed at the source's times after a tool moved the picture in time: pad.py --start 1 kept 0-2 and 2-4, reverse.py kept their order, speedramp.py and fit.py --method speed did not scale them, freeze.py did not push them past the hold, and fit.py --method trim --from-center left them off by the trim
escaped: FFmpeg copies chapters from the first input unless told otherwise, and retimes them only for an input seek, which is why cut.py was right; no test gave a time-changing tool a source with chapters
mechanism: runner.with_mapped_chapters writes the chapters, mapped through the tool's own time map and clipped to the output, as an ffmetadata input of their own (written in the run's private temp directory when the command runs, so a dry run writes nothing) and maps them with -map_chapters; pad, fit, reverse, freeze and speedramp pass their map; test_chapters_follow_a_change_of_time checks the seven cases on Matroska
size_reason: two fixes in one PR: the crop warning is 11 lines; the chapter fix is a helper that writes an ffmetadata input through the run's existing private temp files (so a dry run writes nothing) plus one time map in each of five tools, the smallest place the map is known; no refusal would do it, since keeping the chapters at the wrong times is the defect

what: cut.py --segments, cut.py --remove and silence.py, which join several ranges of one source, kept the source's chapters at the source's times: chapters 0-2 and 2-4 stayed so after 1-2.5 s was removed from a 4 s clip, past the 2.5 s output's end
escaped: found by the class guard of this change, not by a report: the per-tool fix of #696 did not reach the joins, and nothing compared a joined output's chapters with its length
mechanism: the class guard: emit.source_carry says chapters_not_retimed for any output of another length whose tool declared no time map, tests/test_guards.py TimeGuard runs every tool and the multi-range cuts on a chaptered clip and fails on that warning, and docs/defect-guards.json plus revert_proof.py refuse a fix of a class with three or more ledger entries that has no such guard; the joins map their chapters through runner.segments_map, cut's single range and pad --end declare why FFmpeg's own handling is right

what: a request that names an editor's cut (J-cut, L-cut) had no tool: 0 of 6 runs with the skill on three small models answered it, because no tool moved a clip's sound against its picture and nothing in SKILL.md routed the names (a feature, not a defect; recorded because its CHANGELOG entry is read as a fix)
escaped: the cut names were never in the request table, and join.py cut picture and sound at one frame for both streams by construction, so no test asked for a sound that starts before its picture
mechanism: join.py --audio-lead/--audio-lag trim picture and sound at different whole frames of the output rate and concatenate them with one concat filter each; SKILL.md and references/requests.md route the names; test_join_j_cut_starts_the_next_sound_before_its_picture and test_join_l_cut_keeps_the_last_sound_past_the_picture measure the colour of the picture and the tone of the sound at three times each
size_reason: a new option the owner asked for under the freeze (named in code-budget.json): two options, four refusals and the per-clip trims; the ceiling was raised with the reason in code-budget.json

what: audio.py --duck under a speech track longer than its music bed ended the duck at a random point on FFmpeg 7 and later, so the bed came back at full level for the rest of the clip and the file differed from run to run (about 1 run in 8 on FFmpeg 9.0.2 on Windows, 2 of 30)
escaped: sidechaingate forwards the end of its first input without draining the second, and from FFmpeg 7 the command line reads each input on its own thread, so which input ends first became a race; the duck tests used a bed as long as the speech, and no test ran the same command twice
mechanism: duck_graph pads the gated copy of the bed so it never ends before the key, and the mix after it ends with the dry bed (duration=first); test_a_duck_under_a_key_longer_than_its_bed_lasts_to_the_beds_end_on_every_run pins the planned graph, runs the command six times for one output, and measures the duck in the bed's last second

what: an RGB source that probes HDR or BT.2020 reached an encoder whose output tag claimed a matrix the conversion did not use, or lost its tags: export.py --preset youtube and grid.py tagged bt709 over FFmpeg's BT.601 conversion (the red C03028 read CE3E26 by the tag), and --preset prores, dnxhr-*, prores4444, vp9-alpha and graphics/overlay --keep-alpha wrote no primaries, transfer or matrix tag (8-bit DNxHR: bt709 over the same BT.601 pixels)
escaped: #544 fixed the 10-bit HDR line and recorded the 8-bit BT.709 line and the alpha/prores lines as seen and not changed, with bt709_matrix_filter()'s HDR exclusion pinned by a test; the sweep prints what each tool said, and every one of these rows completed with verified true, so only a pixel readback against the source's own code values or ffprobe's tags shows it
mechanism: bt709_matrix_filter() converts an RGB source whatever it probes (the tag on a bt709 line is true), the HDR line keeps hdr_rgb_matrix_filter() and never falls back to the BT.709 one, and one tag helper (decision.hdr_tag_args) writes the matrix, primaries and transfer on every editing master of an HDR source, converted with the matrix it names (hdr_rgb_matrix_filter alpha=True for a YUV alpha line); test_an_hdr_rgb_source_on_a_bt709_line_is_converted_with_the_bt709_matrix and test_an_editing_master_of_an_hdr_rgb_source_keeps_its_tags_and_names_its_matrix read the pixels and the tags back

what: on FFmpeg 9, export.py's BT.709 presets over an HDR source wrote conflicting tags: the encoder's VUI said bt709 and the mp4/mov colr box bt2020/smpte2084 (macOS and Windows CI, FFmpeg 9.0.2), so a player that reads the container treats an SDR-tagged picture as PQ
escaped: from 7.1 the BT.709 tags go into the encoder's VUI to keep libavfilter from converting, and FFmpeg 9 takes the container's colour from the frames, which still carried the source's; the tests that read the tags ran on 6.1 to 8.0 until #708 added one that runs everywhere
mechanism: bt709_matrix_args, the -vf every BT.709 line carries, ends with setparams=color_primaries=bt709:color_trc=bt709 for an HDR source on FFmpeg 9 and later; a probe on 6.1, 7.1, 8.0 and 9.0.2 showed it changes the tags only and no pixel; test_a_bt709_line_relabels_an_hdr_sources_frames_on_ffmpeg_9 pins the args and the youtube readback asserts bt709 three times on every FFmpeg

what: the tools that mix several pictures in one graph (grid, join, multicam, broll, overlay) build each source's BT.709 conversion with matrix_chain, which #712's relabel did not reach: an HDR source in them could still write a bt709 stream under the source's bt2020/PQ container tags on FFmpeg 9
escaped: #712 put the relabel in bt709_matrix_args, the encoder line's -vf, and the mixing tools build their per-source chains through another helper; the sweep that found #711 ran export only
mechanism: one helper, color.bt709_line_filter, is the BT.709 line's filter for both bt709_matrix_args and decision.matrix_chain; the color class reached three entries and has a guard, test_guards.ColorGuard, which runs every tool that writes video plus export's youtube and prores presets, grid and join on an HDR RGB source and fails on an output whose tags mix SDR and HDR (mutation-tested: a bt2020 primaries tag on the BT.709 line fails it)

what: several audio inputs could not become separate named, language-tagged tracks of one file (stems for an NLE package): audio.py wrote one audio stream, mixed or replaced (a feature, not a defect; recorded because its CHANGELOG entry is read as a fix)
escaped: every audio.py mode rebuilds the sound in one filter graph, and no tool wrote a stream per source or a name and language for it
mechanism: audio.py --track maps each source's first audio stream as its own output stream with no filter, and reads names, languages, channels and lengths back from the file (track_tags step, tracks result); the flags that rebuild the sound are refused (track_rebuilds_sound); test_three_tracks_keep_their_channels_lengths_names_and_languages_in_mov_and_mkv and test_a_track_that_a_container_did_not_keep_fails_the_tags_step probe the written file
size_reason: a new option the owner asked for under the freeze (named in code-budget.json): three options, four refusals, a warning and the read-back of each track; the ceiling was raised with the reason in code-budget.json
